ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a rectangular logic function block, with “&” marked inside the block. On the left side there are two ordinary input terminals, labeled A and B respectively; at the lower left there is also an enable terminal labeled EN, at this port a small circle is drawn, and it is connected to constant 0. The output terminal on the right side leads to F, and there is also a small circle at the output terminal. Reasoning: The “&” inside the block means that internally an AND operation is first performed on A and B, obtaining A·B. The EN terminal having a small circle means low-level active enable, and it is connected to 0, so the enable is effectively set, and the function block works normally. The small circle at the output terminal means the output is inverted, therefore F is the inverse of the AND operation result of A and B, namely F = overline(A·B).

method.method_draft: First identify the visual symbols in the circuit. The block contains “&”, so its internal function on inputs A and B is A·B. Check the enable input: EN has a small bubble and is connected to 0, indicating an active-low enable that is asserted, so the gate’s function is valid. Then read the output: the small bubble at the output indicates inversion. Hence the output is the complement of the AND of A and B, giving F = overline(A·B).
